html:
Lempira was a leader of the Lenca people of western Honduras who led a revolt against the Spanish conquest in 1537 and 1538, from a fortified hill called Cerquín.

Spanish settlers had begun to seize land and labour in Honduras after the conquest of the 1520s. Lempira gathered warriors from many Lenca towns and held out for months. By the usual account he was killed during talks with the Spanish, and the revolt then fell apart.

Little is known for certain about him, but he became the national hero of Honduras. Its currency, the lempira, has carried his name since 1931, and a department is named after him. The Lenca still live in the western highlands. His story stands beside that of the K'iche' against Pedro de Alvarado in neighbouring Guatemala.
sum: Lempira was a leader of the Lenca people of western Honduras who led a revolt against the Spanish conquest in 1537 and 1538, from a fortified hill called Cerquín.
